scope: Append-only screen of additional 1100-1500 candidates. The records preserve useful population, pressure, food-system and technology evidence while refusing to create a training target when a closed local-food boundary, saturation interval or independent upper endpoint is missing.

promotion_audit.decision: No new global scale anchor is promoted in this wave. Catalonia and Mallorca are explicitly rejected because their observations are urban/fiscal or import-dependent; Bali and Sri Lanka are retained as physical validation cases because no defensible medieval population interval and saturation fraction were found.
promotion_audit.review_method: Checked date compatibility, population semantics, local-food dependence, pressure evidence, shock/trade confounds, historical boundary definition and EU5 crosswalkability. No starting population, HYDE, RGO or modern population field is used.
required_followup: Catalonia: reconstruct a medieval rural boundary and obtain an enumerated or archaeological population interval with independent marginal-land/real-wage pressure evidence; resolve urban and migration shares.
Mallorca: find a same-boundary rural population series and saturation evidence; quantify or remove imported Atlantic wheat before any local-food capacity use.
Bali: locate a dated 1100-1500 population or carrying-capacity interval for the mapped subak/rice landscape and a historical boundary polygon.
Sri Lanka dry zone: map the tank-system footprint and obtain a dated population interval plus evidence separating irrigation abandonment, warfare and climate shocks from equilibrium capacity.

records.label: Catalonia c.1290-1329: demographic pressure and famine, but no closed local-food capacity interval
records.interval_semantics: The approximately 500,000 figure around 1300 is a broad historical reconstruction, not an enumeration and not a carrying-capacity interval. It includes urban and market-town populations and cannot be assigned to an autarkic rural boundary.
pressure_evidence: Enciclopedia Catalana places Catalonia near approximately 500,000 inhabitants around 1300 and describes the subsequent demographic crisis; the same discussion warns that fiscal fogatges are not direct population enumerations.
The Crown of Aragon literature documents grain-market intervention and recurrent dearth/famine in the early fourteenth century, consistent with pressure but not with a measured saturation fraction.
A modern famine synthesis treats population pressure as a possible remote driver of famine; it does not provide a Catalonia boundary-matched equilibrium estimate.
shock_flags: broad fiscal reconstructions and fogatges may undercount or change taxable units
Barcelona and other market towns redistribute grain from outside the immediate rural footprint
migration and urbanization are not separable at the available aggregate boundary
records.trade_dependence: mixed_to_high; Crown of Aragon grain markets and coastal redistribution are documented but local share is not quantified
records.food_regime: Mediterranean cereals, legumes, vines, olives, livestock and coastal fisheries with market redistribution
records.boundary_description: Catalonia as a broad medieval principality/modern-region envelope; no audited rural-only 1290-1329 polygon is available and the political boundary changed over the interval.
records.source_family_independence: Independent regional-history and famine literature; the record is excluded for unresolved boundary/population semantics rather than treated as a synthetic label.
citation_details: Enciclopedia Catalana: approximately 500,000 around 1300 and a later crisis; fiscal fogatges are treated as an imperfect demographic proxy.
Crown of Aragon grain-market and famine studies: market intervention and dearth are pressure context, not a saturation endpoint.
Nature Sustainability famine synthesis: population pressure is a general risk mechanism, not a Catalonia-specific capacity measurement.
records.notes: Rejected from training. Promotion requires a mappable rural boundary, independently bounded population, quantified local-food share and upper saturation evidence. Keep as a test that imported or urban food is not assigned to surrounding intrinsic capacity.

records.label: Mallorca c.1301-1329: exact island and fiscal observations, but chronic Atlantic wheat imports invalidate a local-food target
records.interval_semantics: The 1329 estimate of approximately 56,000 is a historical population point with a broad review range, while the 1301 morabeti is a taxable-household count. Neither supplies a saturation interval or a rural-only local-food population.
pressure_evidence: The 1301 morabeti tax was a fiscal assessment of taxable households, not a complete headcount; scholarly discussion warns against treating it as a direct population enumeration.

A historical Mallorca food-system study identifies a persistent wheat deficit and Atlantic wheat imports between 1230 and 1350, directly violating the local-food requirement for an intrinsic capacity label.
The 1329 population estimate and later decline are useful for a shock-sensitive island validation case, but do not identify equilibrium saturation.
shock_flags: 1329-1421 famine/epidemic decline overlaps the source series and extends beyond 1337
morabeti taxable-household semantics and possible under-registration
Palma urban and port population is embedded in the island estimate
documented Atlantic wheat imports and maritime redistribution
records.trade_dependence: high_import_dependence; Atlantic wheat imports are documented for 1230-1350
records.food_regime: Mediterranean cereals, legumes, vines, olives, livestock, fisheries and imported wheat
records.boundary_description: Mallorca island boundary is geographically exact, but the population sources do not separate Palma/ports from rural hinterland and no saturation fraction is published.
records.source_family_independence: Independent island demographic, fiscal and food-trade sources; the record is rejected because imported calories and fiscal semantics prevent a local-food target.
citation_details: Morabeti study: the 1301 assessment is a fiscal taxable-household instrument, not a complete population census.
Sustainability (2019): approximately 56,000 people in 1329 and island-wide famine/epidemic decline after 1329.
Mallorca and Atlantic wheat (1230-1350): persistent wheat deficit and import dependence.
records.notes: Rejected from training. Keep as a negative control for islands: the physical model may estimate intrinsic land capacity, but observed Mallorca population cannot calibrate it without removing imported wheat and separating urban/port food flows.

records.label: Bali subak rice terraces c.1100-1500: durable irrigation evidence without a medieval population/saturation interval
records.interval_semantics: Subak inscriptions and archaeological terrace evidence establish a long-lived local irrigation institution, but the reviewed sources provide no dated 1100-1500 population interval or saturation fraction for a closed mapped landscape.
pressure_evidence: UNESCO describes the subak cooperative irrigation system and rice terraces as a centuries-old landscape, with institutional origins in the ninth century and later royal management.
Archaeological and historical studies identify subak by eleventh-century royal inscriptions and link water-sharing institutions to intensive rice production.
The evidence supports technology feasibility and local-food production effects, not an equilibrium population target.
shock_flags: modern terrace area and population density cannot be back-projected to 1337
subak catchments are distributed temple/watershed units rather than one documented medieval aggregate boundary
no independent famine, marginal-land, wage or abandonment evidence resolves saturation
later colonial and modern irrigation expansion confounds observed extent
records.trade_dependence: unresolved; local rice is documented but regional exchange share is not
records.food_regime: irrigated rice, dry-field crops, tubers, livestock, freshwater foods and forest products
records.boundary_description: Multiple Bali subak and watershed catchments; no single 1100-1500 population-bearing polygon was reconstructed from the reviewed sources.
records.source_family_independence: Independent archaeological, inscriptional and landscape sources; no modern population value is used as a medieval label.
citation_details: UNESCO World Heritage: subak water temples and rice terraces; institutional origins are traced to at least the ninth century.
Niche-construction and geography studies: eleventh-century inscriptions and water-sharing institutions support pre-1337 irrigated rice feasibility.
No source supplies a closed-boundary medieval population or saturation interval.
records.notes: Validation-only physical case. It can test irrigation reach, crop-date masks and land-allocation behavior once a Bali crosswalk exists, but it cannot supervise global scale without a dated population and pressure interval.

records.label: Sri Lanka dry-zone tank systems c.1100-1302: strong irrigation technology evidence, but no closed population/saturation anchor
records.interval_semantics: The Polonnaruwa-era tank cascade and irrigation governance are documented, including abandonment and later restoration, but no same-boundary population interval or equilibrium saturation fraction is available in the reviewed sources.
pressure_evidence: The Tank Systems of the Dry Zone project documents village tanks, cascade governance, paddy fields and water allocation as a durable local-food system.
Archaeological and historical work records cycles of urbanization/de-urbanization and tank abandonment, showing that maintenance and political shocks affected production.
The physical evidence is suitable for irrigation and water-budget validation, not for inventing a population target from tank counts or modern densities.
shock_flags: war, political fragmentation and tank-maintenance failure are not separable from ecological carrying capacity
Polonnaruwa urban and administrative population is not a rural catchment label
no audited historical tank-cascade polygon matched to EU5 geometry
records.trade_dependence: unresolved; paddy local-food production is documented but state redistribution is not quantified
records.food_regime: irrigated paddy, dry-field grains, pulses, livestock, fisheries and tank/wetland foods
records.boundary_description: Dry-zone tank cascades around Polonnaruwa and adjacent village systems; the reviewed sources do not provide one closed 1100-1302 rural aggregate polygon.
records.source_family_independence: Independent irrigation archaeology and governance sources; no population or modern land-use statistic is promoted to a medieval target.
citation_details: Tank Systems of the Dry Zone project: village tanks, cascades, water allocation and abandonment/maintenance history.
Archaeological review: cycles of de-urbanization and adaptation; irrigation infrastructure is evidence of capability, not an equilibrium headcount.
No source supplies a closed rural population interval or saturation fraction for 1100-1302.
records.notes: Validation-only physical case. Promote only after a historical tank-system polygon, dated population interval and independent pressure/saturation evidence are resolved.
